title: A novel method for the collection of highly developmental murine immature oocytes
author: Taiyeb

steps.title: Recover GV‑stage oocytes
steps.instruction: Collect germinal‑vesicle (GV) oocytes from super‑ovulated Swiss Webster females using a two‑dose cilostazol regimen.

substeps.instruction: Prime each female mouse intraperitoneally (i.p.) with 5 IU pregnant mare serum gonadotropin (PMSG) to stimulate follicle development.
Exactly 47 h after the PMSG injection, inject 5 IU human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) i.p. to induce ovulation.

Prepare the first 7.5 mg cilostazol dose: dissolve 7.5 mg cilostazol in 0.1 mL warm dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), vortex for 1 min, aspirate into an insulin syringe, attach a gavage tube, and gavage the mouse at the same time as the hCG injection. Adjust the volume so that the amount remaining in the gavage tube is accounted for.
Prepare a second identical 7.5 mg cilostazol dose (same 0.1 mL warm DMSO, vortex 1 min) and gavage the mouse 6 h after the hCG injection.
Alternative dosing (optional): give a single 7.5 mg cilostazol dose dissolved in 0.1 mL warm DMSO 4 h before hCG and a second dose 2 h after hCG.
At 13–14 h post‑hCG, sacrifice the mouse by cervical dislocation under appropriate anesthesia.

Make a peritoneal incision, excise ovaries, oviducts, and a segment of the uterine horn, and place them immediately in 2 mL warm human tubal fluid (HTF) medium supplemented with HEPES, 4.5 % fetal bovine serum (FBS), and 4.2 µM cilostazol (add only if you wish to block spontaneous meiotic maturation).
Under a stereomicroscope, puncture the distended ampulla of each oviduct with a 30‑gauge needle to release cumulus‑enclosed oocytes at the GV stage.

steps.title: Recover MI‑stage oocytes
steps.instruction: Collect metaphase‑I (MI) oocytes from super‑ovulated Swiss Webster females using a single cilostazol gavage.

substeps.instruction: Prime each female mouse i.p. with 5 IU PMSG to stimulate follicle development.
Exactly 47 h after the PMSG injection, inject 5 IU hCG i.p. to induce ovulation.

Prepare a 7.5 mg cilostazol dose: dissolve 7.5 mg cilostazol in 0.1 mL warm DMSO, vortex for 1 min, aspirate into an insulin syringe, attach a gavage tube, and gavage the mouse either at the same time as the hCG injection or 4 h before hCG.
At 13–14 h post‑hCG, sacrifice the mouse by cervical dislocation under appropriate anesthesia.

After a peritoneal incision, place ovaries, oviducts, and a piece of the uterine horn in 2 mL warm HTF medium supplemented with HEPES, 4.5 % FBS, and 4.2 µM cilostazol (optional, to block spontaneous maturation).
Using a stereomicroscope, puncture the distended ampulla with a 30‑gauge needle to release cumulus‑enclosed oocytes at the MI stage.
Alternative: obtain MI oocytes by in‑vitro maturation (IVM) of ovulated GV oocytes harvested from mice that received the two‑dose cilostazol regimen described for GV recovery.

description: Collection of immature oocytes from superovulated mice treated with cilostazol has resulted in immature oocytes that are more (a) uniform in size, (b) ready to undergo GVBD or first polar body emission, (c) synchronized with nuclear and cytoplasmic development, (d) competent, (e) and capable of producing live births than did control immature or mature oocytes [17], [18], [19]. The presented method is also characterized by ease of collection and processing, time-saving, and convenience in comparison to the conventional method. Finally, the cilostazol method results in high oocyte yield per mouse in comparison to immature oocytes recovered using the conventional method [15].
